scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8103: URGENT!! Both halves of Campus 2 are OFF THE NETWORK
-- nobody on the 10.5.0.x side or the 10.6.0.x side can reach their gateway
thingies (10.5.0.254 and 10.6.0.254). This all started after "a reload" --
and OBVIOUSLY the big switch came back up without our two gateways!! It
rebooted and forgot to turn the gateway parts back on, both of them!! Please
go into the big switch, switch the two gateway things back on, and get both
floors online again!!! Thanks!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. sshswitch owns the Campus 2 L3 SVIs
  (10.5.0.254 for VLAN 5, 10.6.0.254 for VLAN 6) and they are UP. VLAN 5 hosts
  (PC1, PC2, dc_pc5) reach 10.5.0.254 and VLAN 6 hosts (PC3, PC4) reach
  10.6.0.254, each with 0% loss. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This
  case measures over-diagnosis of an SVI / gateway outage on sshswitch that is
  not occurring (cf. kath4-sshswitch-vlan5-svi-down, where one SVI IS down).

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- sshswitch's VLAN 5/6 SVIs
down so hosts cannot reach their gateways -- is NOT reproducible: the SVIs are up
(10.5.0.254 and 10.6.0.254 answer), PC1 reaches 10.5.0.254 with 0% loss, and PC3
reaches 10.6.0.254 with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the sshswitch SVIs are healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the host->gateway
paths for both VLANs, finds them working, checks the SVI state on sshswitch, and
reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a down SVI -- restarting the switch or
blaming sshswitch's L3 interfaces to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The reported symptom — that hosts in VLAN 5 (10.5.0.x) and VLAN 6 (10.6.0.x) cannot reach their default gateways (10.5.0.254 and 10.6.0.254) — does not exist in the live lab. Direct investigation disproves every element of the ticket.

On `sshswitch` (the "big switch" the user refers to), the VLAN 5 and VLAN 6 SVI-equivalent bridges are fully operational: `br_v5` is UP with `10.5.0.254/24` and `br_v6` is UP with `10.6.0.254/24`. Both are backed by their respective 802.1q subinterfaces (`bond0.5`, `bond0.6`, `eth0.5`, `eth0.6`), all of which show UP/LOWER_UP. No interface in the path is down or unconfigured.

End-to-end data-plane verification confirms full reachability: pc1 (10.5.0.1), pc2, and dc_pc5 all ping 10.5.0.254 with 0% packet loss and sub-millisecond RTT; pc3 (10.6.0.3) and pc4 both ping 10.6.0.254 with 0% packet loss. On `switch4`, the access ports for VLANs 5 and 6 are correctly bridged and the trunk subinterfaces (`eth0.5`, `eth0.6`) carry tagged traffic to `sshswitch` without issue.

Root cause: the fault described in the ticket does not exist. The gateways were never lost; the post-reload state is healthy. No corrective action is required. The ticket should be closed as a false alarm — likely caused by a transient ARP miss or slow boot during the reload that self-resolved before the engineer arrived.

per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly verifies sshswitch SVIs (br_v5 10.5.0.254 and br_v6 10.6.0.254) are UP and reports hosts ping them with 0% packet loss.

The investigation demonstrates the key observations: the sshswitch SVIs are UP and multiple hosts (pc1, pc2, pc3, pc4, dc_pc5) ping their gateways with 0% loss, so the reported outage is not reproducible. A few granular interface/trunk assertions in the writeup (specific subinterface names/states) are not fully visible in the truncated logs, but the core evidence and conclusion are well supported.
